title: From “let’s see what AI can do” to “I make games now”: my 5 stages
author: Dapper-Business5405
selftext:
Hi everybody 👋

Last week some of you told me to go isometric, thanks again for that! Today I want to share something different: how I went from "let's see what AI can really do" to "I make games now". The picture shows my game Kiosk Days at each stage.

(1) At the end of August I just wanted to see what Claude Code can do, partly also for my job. I told it about a trading game I played as a kid on MS-DOS (Imbiss Manager, still with ASCII graphics) and how I imagine it today. That was the first version: plain HTML, only numbers and sliders.

(2) It worked better than I expected, so I wanted more and more and just kept chatting. A little kiosk drawn in CSS, new features, everything in one long chat.

(3) At some point I noticed that Claude always took the easiest way and built everything itself. So I asked: "Isn't there something that already exists that you can use?" That's how I ended up with Phaser and a world to walk around, and a few days later with Godot. For me that was the first big lesson: the AI doesn't ask these questions, I have to.

(4) My biggest mistake was the 3D version. For two weeks I only wrote specs and let Claude work, without playing it once. When I finally played it, the controls were complicated and it just didn't feel like my game anymore. So I went back to 2D. Since then I play my game every day.

(5) Today it's not one chat anymore, it's kind of a small team. Every game has its own skills, for example one that draws all the pixel art with Python scripts (no image generator for the sprites). I also had a reviewer agent that ran all tests after each bigger change. I have three games now, so they share one queue for AI images and sound, and one session works through it, so they don't fight over the Gemini limit. Because I always lost track of which session was waiting for me, I let Claude build a "Claude Manager": a web page where I see all my sessions and answer their questions, even from my phone 😄 And there is even a session for marketing: it plans posts, reads my numbers on itch, TikTok and YouTube and writes drafts, like this post (I'm not a native English speaker). I still decide and post myself.

(6) - not yet ready: the isometric view. After this is still in progres, there is not Screenshot 😄 

Three months ago I only wanted to try it out. Now I'm making games.

What does your setup look like? Are you still in one long chat, or do you also use skills and agents? And did you also have a moment where the AI took the easy way and you only noticed later?



If you want to see where the game is now: [https://kigaro-games.itch.io/kiosk-days](https://kigaro-games.itch.io/kiosk-days)
